title: Handwashing & Self-Care
strapline: Sleeves up, taps on, bubbles between the fingers — turning a health routine into a warm little ritual a child can own.
intent: Help toddlers learn to wash and dry their own hands, wipe their own noses and manage the small self-care of the day.
Build the sequence and independence of a health routine — sleeves up, wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry — that lasts a lifetime.
Develop the fine-motor and body-awareness skills of turning taps, rubbing hands, pulling a towel, blowing a nose.
Grow understanding of why we care for our bodies — before snack, after the garden, when we've sneezed — without fear or fuss.
Make self-care a calm, unhurried, even enjoyable ritual, woven into the rhythm of the day.
implementation: Set up child-height sinks or a step, with soap they can pump, a low towel or paper within reach, and a mirror for nose-wiping.
Model and narrate the sequence warmly, singing a handwashing song so the timing and the steps become familiar.
Build handwashing into the natural moments — before eating, after the toilet, after outdoor and messy play — so it becomes routine, not a battle.
Offer a tissue box at child height and teach the wipe-and-bin, giving toddlers ownership of their own runny noses.
Keep it playful and pressure-free — bubbles to make, a song to finish, a mirror to check — never a scolding.
key_questions: What do we do first — shall we push our sleeves up?
Can you make lots of bubbles between your fingers?
Why do we wash our hands before snack?
How will you dry them — all the way, even between the fingers?
Your nose needs a wipe — can you do it and pop the tissue in the bin?

impact.text: Children wash and dry their own hands and wipe their own noses, managing real self-care with growing independence.
A toddler pushes up sleeves, works the tap and rubs in the soap themselves — 'me do it!' — proud to manage the whole routine.
Children anticipate the familiar routine — sleeves up before the tap, hands before snack — knowing what comes next.
Turning taps and pumping soap, toddlers explore how these everyday things work.

enhancements: A child-height sink or a sturdy step with a pump soap and low towel.
A handwashing song card or picture sequence above the basin.
A mirror at the sink for checking a clean face and a wiped nose.
A low tissue box and a 'catch it, bin it' picture prompt.
Glitter-and-oil 'germs' demonstration on a warm day to show why soap matters.

playing_exploring: Children explore soap, bubbles and water at the sink, enjoying the sensation as they wash.
The routine is learned hands-on, step by familiar step.
active_learning: Toddlers take pride in managing more of the sequence themselves each time, wanting to do it alone.
creating_thinking: Children hold the order in mind — sleeves, wet, soap, rinse, dry — and carry it out from memory.
